identity.title: Pulse deficit / asymmetric radial, carotid or femoral pulses

technique.how: Palpate both radial pulses simultaneously, then both femoral (and carotid) pulses, comparing amplitude and timing side to side. A deficit is an absent or clearly weaker pulse on one side, or a radial-femoral lag; confirm with bilateral BP or Doppler if uncertain.
technique.prerequisites: Accessible limbs; note prior vascular surgery, arterial lines, or known peripheral arterial disease.
technique.contraindications: Avoid firm bilateral carotid palpation at the same time.

interpretation.positive_finding: A new unilateral pulse deficit in a patient with acute chest/back/abdominal pain strongly increases the probability of aortic dissection (pooled LR+ 5.7; ED case-control LR+ 31, specificity 99.3%).
interpretation.negative_finding: Normal symmetric pulses do not exclude dissection: only 15-31% of confirmed dissections have a pulse deficit.
interpretation.pitfalls: Chronic peripheral arterial disease, prior catheterization, or subclavian stenosis cause asymmetric pulses without dissection; deficits can be intermittent as the false lumen shifts, so re-examine.
interpretation.changes_what: New pulse deficit with suspicious pain: treat as dissection until imaged (CTA/TEE); absence changes little and should not lower suspicion.

estimates.population: Consecutive patients with confirmed thoracic aortic dissection across 21 studies (pooled; pulse deficit or BP differential combined)
estimates.reference_standard: Imaging/surgery/autopsy-confirmed dissection in the primary studies
estimates.quote: 31% have pulse deficits or blood pressure differentials … differentials and neurological deficits increase the likelihood of disease (positive LRs, 5.7 and 6.6-33.0, respectively)

estimates.population: Adults >18 y with nontraumatic truncal pain; matched case-control (194 AAD cases, 776 controls)
estimates.reference_standard: CT or echocardiography-confirmed AAD vs truncal-pain controls without clear diagnosis

estimates.target_condition: Acute aortic dissection (type A and B)
estimates.population: 464 patients with confirmed acute aortic dissection enrolled in IRAD registry, 12 referral centers
estimates.reference_standard: Confirmed acute aortic dissection (registry case series; no controls)
estimates.quote: Classic physical findings such as aortic regurgitation and pulse deficit were noted in only 31.6% and 15.1% of patients, respectively

sources.citation: Klompas M. Does this patient have an acute thoracic aortic dissection? JAMA. 2002;287(17):2262-2272.
Ohle R, Kareemi HK, Wells G, Perry JJ. High Risk Clinical Features for Acute Aortic Dissection: A Case-Control Study. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(4):378-387.
Hagan PG, Nienaber CA, Isselbacher EM, et al. The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD): new insights into an old disease. JAMA. 2000;283(7):897-903.
Ohle R, Um J, Anjum O, et al. Clinical Examination for Acute Aortic Dissection: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(4):397-412.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not interpret asymmetry in patients with known peripheral arterial disease, prior arterial access, or arm AV fistula without Doppler/BP confirmation.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: New pulse deficit with acute pain, hypotension, or neuro deficit = immediate CTA/TEE and surgical consult; do not delay for further bedside tests.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Palpation-based; Klompas pooled sensitivity spans 10-40% across studies (heterogeneity noted in RCE), reflecting definition and examiner variability.

extraction_notes: Estimate 0: Klompas 2002 RCE pooled sensitivity 31% and LR+ 5.7 for 'pulse deficits or blood pressure differentials' combined (abstract); the two numbers come from two separate abstract sentences, quoted as two fragments joined by an ellipsis; specificity and CI not in abstract (full-text table not accessible). Estimate 1: Ohle 2018 ED case-control, pulse deficit alone: specificity 99.3%, LR+ 31.1 (11.2-86.6); sensitivity not in abstract. Estimate 2: IRAD registry sensitivity 15.1% (case series, no controls, so no LR). Ohle 2018 meta-analysis (source 3) mentions pulse deficit qualitatively in its abstract without a pooled number, so cited as context only. Range in interobserver_note is descriptive of heterogeneity across RCE-included studies as summarized in my reading of the abstract-level data; no kappa found.
